trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud to the city center (budget tip: Metro costs ~€5.50 vs Aerobus ~€6.75 — both affordable). Check into Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a relaxed walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — see Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Marvel at Gaudí's iconic facades without spending a euro.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to Plaça de Catalunya to get your bearings and soak in the city atmosphere. Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) for an evening wander through its atmospheric medieval streets — completely free. Grab dinner nearby and then enjoy a drink at one of the lively bars in El Born neighborhood, which comes alive after 9 PM.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — arrival is at 13:00
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bocadillo (sandwich) from a local bakery or Mercadona supermarket near Eixample for €2–4
meals.dinner: Bar Calders in Sant Antoni neighborhood — tapas-style pintxos and affordable raciones, budget ~€10–14 per person with a drink

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip Metro card (~€12.15) upon arrival — it covers all Metro, bus, and tram rides and is the best budget transport option. August evenings are warm (~25°C), perfect for outdoor strolling.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to La Sagrada Família — book tickets online in advance to save time and potentially get a discount slot (~€26 basic entry). Arrive when it opens at 9:00 AM to beat the August crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, the most iconic piece of architecture in Barcelona. The towers offer stunning city views for an extra fee (~€36 with tower access).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the Metro to Park Güell (book free community zone access or pay ~€10 for the Monumental Zone). Spend 1.5 hours exploring Gaudí's colorful mosaic terraces and organic architecture with sweeping views over the city. Afterward, head back toward Gràcia neighborhood and browse the charming Mercat de l'Abaceria or explore the bohemian squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia — all free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and explore the vibrant Gayxample area around Carrer del Consell de Cent. This is Barcelona's LGBTQ+ hub but universally welcoming, with great bars and affordable pre-dinner drinks. Enjoy the classic Barcelona evening ritual of 'vermut' (vermouth) at a local bar around 7–8 PM before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Federal or a local bar near Eixample — café amb llet (coffee with milk) and a tostada con tomate (toast with tomato) for ~€3–5
meals.lunch: Menú del día (set lunch menu) near Park Güell or Gràcia — 3 courses with bread and drink for €11–14, the best budget deal in Spain
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — popular spot with excellent pintxos and tapas, budget ~€12–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book both Sagrada Família and Park Güell online at least a week ahead — August is peak season and timed entry slots sell out fast. Wear comfortable shoes as both sites involve significant walking.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) for a self-guided architecture walk. Visit the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 PM on weekdays), explore the ancient Roman ruins visible through glass floors at Plaça del Rei, and wander through Carrer del Bisbe with its neo-Gothic bridge. Cross into El Born to see the stunning Santa Maria del Mar church (free or ~€5 with audioguide) — a perfect example of Catalan Gothic architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit La Barceloneta beach for a few hours — it's free and just a 20-minute walk from El Born. Cool off in the Mediterranean and enjoy the beach scene. Afterward, walk along the Port Olímpic waterfront and admire Frank Gehry's giant golden 'Peix' (Fish) sculpture — a striking piece of contemporary architecture. Explore the Poblenou neighborhood on the way back, Barcelona's up-and-coming creative district with street art and converted factory architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Poblenou and the Rambla del Poblenou come alive at night. This is a more local, less touristy nightlife scene. Start with drinks at a terrace bar around 9 PM, then head to one of the area's clubs or live music venues after midnight. Razzmatazz (a legendary multi-room club in Poblenou) is one of Barcelona's best nightlife institutions — entry ~€15–20.

meals.breakfast: El Xampanyet in El Born — a classic old-school bar, grab a coffee and pastry for ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Barceloneta beach chiringuito (beach bar) — fresh grilled fish or a bocadillo, budget ~€8–12
meals.dinner: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, no reservations) — legendary local spot said to have invented the bombas (potato croquettes), very affordable at ~€10–13

day_by_day.notes: Barcelona nightlife rarely starts before midnight — don't arrive at clubs before 1 AM. Keep valuables secure in the Gothic Quarter and on Las Ramblas, which are popular pickpocket areas. Bring a beach towel from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Montjuïc hill. Ride the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car (~€12.70 return) for panoramic views of the city and port — a spectacular sight. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) for more views and history. Then explore the Fundació Joan Miró (~€14) — a world-class modern art museum housed in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert, set among beautiful gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Montjuïc or take the cable car back and head to the Pavillon Mies van der Rohe (~€7) — a reconstructed modernist masterpiece that is a must-see for architecture enthusiasts. Then visit the nearby Parc de Joan Miró to see his giant sculpture 'Dona i Ocell' for free. Spend the rest of the afternoon exploring the Sant Antoni neighborhood, known for its beautifully restored Mercat de Sant Antoni (free to browse) and indie bookshops.
day_by_day.evening: Sant Antoni is one of Barcelona's trendiest evening spots. Join locals for vermouth hour at one of the many bars surrounding the market. Later, explore the nightlife on Carrer del Parlament and Carrer de la Riera Alta — lively bars with a young, local crowd and affordable drinks. This area is more authentic than the tourist-heavy Gothic Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in Sant Antoni — excellent brunch spot, budget ~€6–9 for coffee and avocado toast or eggs
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni — grab fresh produce, cheese, and cured meats for a DIY picnic on Montjuïc, budget ~€5–8
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda near Sant Antoni — rustic wine bar with affordable tapas and excellent house wine, budget ~€10–14

day_by_day.notes: The Fundació Joan Miró offers free entry on Saturdays after 3 PM — check their current schedule to save money. Montjuïc is very exposed in August heat; bring water and sunscreen. The hill is also the site of the 1992 Olympic Stadium, free to walk around.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most extraordinary pieces of Modernista architecture in the world by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Book a guided tour (~€22) or attend a morning concert if available (tickets vary). The stained-glass skylight and ornate facade are breathtaking. Afterward, explore the surrounding El Born neighborhood's boutique shops and street art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mercat de la Boqueria on Las Ramblas for a final browse — it's touristy but iconic. Resist overpriced stalls at the front and head to the back for better prices. Pick up local products like Manchego cheese, jamón, or olives as souvenirs. Spend your last afternoon revisiting a favorite neighborhood or checking out the free MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona) plaza, a hub of skate culture and street life, and admire the stark white building by Richard Meier.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Eixample, close to the hotel. Splurge slightly on your last night or stick to the budget — either way, enjoy a proper Catalan meal. After dinner, take one last evening walk along Passeig de Gràcia to see Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) illuminated at night — both are stunning after dark and completely free to admire from outside.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a classic Spanish breakfast at a local bar near Eixample — café con leche and churros con chocolate for ~€4–6
meals.lunch: Mercat de la Boqueria — fresh fruit, a slice of tortilla española, and a juice for ~€6–10 (avoid the tourist-facing counters)
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza in Eixample — beloved local spot with excellent Neapolitan-style pizza in a lively setting, budget ~€12–16 per person including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Pack and prepare for departure the night before if your flight is early. Store luggage at the hotel if you have a late flight — most hotels offer this service free of charge. The Metro to the airport runs from Passeig de Gràcia station. Total estimated 5-day budget per person (excluding flights): €200–280, including accommodation, food, transport, and key attraction entries.

trip_options.title: Classic Barcelona Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via Aerobus or taxi (~30–40 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along Passeig de Gràcia from the hotel to admire the iconic Manzana de la Discordia block — spot Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller from the outside at no cost. This gentle walk eases you into Barcelona's stunning Modernista streetscape right from your doorstep in Eixample.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Eixample Esquerra (left side) bar scene known as 'Gayxample' for pre-dinner drinks, then settle in for a relaxed first dinner at a neighborhood restaurant. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a quick coffee and croissant at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample institution serving excellent tapas and montaditos at mid-range prices (€15–20/person).
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza on Londres street — a stylish, casual Eixample spot with wood-fired pizzas and natural wines; great value for a low-key first evening (€20–25/person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card at the airport or a nearby metro station to save on transport throughout the trip. August in Barcelona is hot (30°C+), so carry water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Book the first entry slot (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and the midday heat. The guided tour (~1.5–2 hrs) reveals Gaudí's extraordinary symbolism across the Nativity and Passion facades, the stunning interior forest of columns, and the towers with panoramic views. Pre-book tickets online (€26–35/person with tower access).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration. Take the metro to Lesseps or Vallcarca and walk up to Gaudí's whimsical hilltop park. Explore the monumental zone with its iconic mosaic terrace and Hypostyle Room (ticket required, ~€10). Afterward, wind down through the charming bohemian Gràcia neighborhood — browse its village-like squares (Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia) and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for a relaxed evening. Enjoy aperitivo hour (vermouth time) at a classic bar before dinner, a beloved Barcelona tradition especially on weekdays.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in Sant Antoni (short walk from Eixample) — excellent avocado toast, eggs, and specialty coffee; a Barcelona brunch institution (€10–15/person). Go early before the Sagrada Família visit.
meals.lunch: Picnic from a Gràcia neighborhood deli or grab a menú del día (set lunch) at a local restaurant in Gràcia — typically €12–15 for starter, main, dessert, and drink. Try Plaça de la Virreina area.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample — a cozy wine bar and restaurant with Catalan small plates and an excellent wine list at mid-range prices (€25–35/person).

day_by_day.notes: Sagrada Família tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online immediately if not already done. Wear comfortable shoes for Park Güell's uneven mosaic paths. The Gràcia neighborhood is particularly lively in mid-August during its famous Festa Major de Gràcia street festival (check exact 2027 dates — typically mid-August).

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — Start at 9:30 AM before the heat peaks. Begin at the Barcelona Cathedral, explore the Roman ruins visible through glass floors at the MUHBA City History Museum (€7), then weave through the labyrinthine Gothic Quarter streets. Cross into El Born to admire the stunning iron Mercat de Santa Caterina and the Santa Maria del Mar basilica — one of the finest examples of Catalan Gothic architecture in Europe (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience — Walk up La Rambla to La Boqueria for a mid-afternoon visit (slightly less crowded than morning). Sample fresh fruit juices, jamón ibérico, Catalan cheeses, and pintxos from market stalls. Browse without pressure to buy everything — this is as much a sensory experience as a meal. Afterward, relax at a café in El Raval or return to the hotel for a siesta — essential in August heat.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Club & Nightlife on Passeig Marítim — Head to Barceloneta beach for the golden hour. Start with sunset cocktails at a chiringuito (beach bar) around 8:00 PM. Dine at a seafood restaurant on the waterfront, then join the Passeig Marítim nightlife scene — beach clubs like Opium or Pacha open late (midnight onwards) for those wanting to dance.

meals.breakfast: Bar del Pla in El Born — a local favorite for coffee and a croissant or tostada con tomate (bread rubbed with tomato and olive oil, a Catalan staple) for €5–8.
meals.lunch: Graze through La Boqueria stalls for a self-curated lunch of market tapas, fresh seafood, and local specialties — budget €15–20 for a satisfying spread.
meals.dinner: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, no reservations — arrive early) — the legendary birthplace of the bombas (potato croquettes) and fresh seafood. Extremely authentic and affordable (€20–25/person). Alternatively, La Mar Salada for a slightly more refined waterfront seafood experience (€35–45/person).

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is very touristy — avoid buying prepared seafood dishes at inflated stall prices; stick to fresh produce and cured meats. La Cova Fumada closes early afternoon and has no sign — look it up on maps in advance. Beach clubs have cover charges (€15–20) that often include a drink. Bring a light layer for late-night sea breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill Morning — Take the cable car or bus up to Montjuïc for cooler morning air and sweeping city views. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14) for world-class modern art in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert — a must for architecture lovers. Walk the castle grounds of Castell de Montjuïc for panoramic harbor views (€5 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Palau Nacional & Poble Sec — Descend to the Palau Nacional (home of the MNAC museum, €12) to see its extraordinary Romanesque art collection and the grand architecture of the 1929 World Exposition buildings. Walk down through Poble Sec, a hip residential neighborhood with a thriving local food and bar scene on Carrer de Blai (famous for its pintxos bars). Rest at the hotel before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Nightlife & Cocktail Bar Crawl — Explore the sophisticated cocktail bar scene in Eixample. Start at Bar Calders in Sant Antoni for vermouth, move to Mutis for creative cocktails, and finish at one of the rooftop bars like the Almanac Hotel rooftop for skyline views. This is a more refined, local nightlife experience compared to the beach clubs.

meals.breakfast: Cafè de l'Acadèmia near the Gothic Quarter or a local Eixample bakery — coffee, fresh orange juice, and a croissant or ensaïmada (Catalan pastry) for €6–10.
meals.lunch: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl in Poble Sec — grab rounds of pintxos (Basque-style bar snacks on bread) from multiple bars at €1.50–2 each; a fun, social, and affordable lunch (€12–18 total).
meals.dinner: Bodega 1900 by Albert Adrià in Poble Sec (book in advance) — a creative reinvention of a traditional Spanish vermouth bar with elevated tapas; mid-to-upper mid-range (€40–55/person). Or opt for Tickets (same group, requires advance booking) for a more theatrical experience.

day_by_day.notes: Book Bodega 1900 or Tickets well in advance — Albert Adrià's restaurants fill up fast. The Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) offers spectacular views and is worth the €12.70 round-trip cost. Wednesday evenings in Eixample tend to be lively without the extreme weekend crowds — a great balance for nightlife exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana Guided Tour — Begin your final full day with this UNESCO World Heritage concert hall, a breathtaking Art Nouveau masterpiece by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The guided tour (€22, ~55 min) reveals the extraordinary stained glass, ceramic mosaics, and sculptural details. If lucky, check for morning concerts — attending a performance here is unforgettable. Located in El Born, easily walkable from the Gothic Quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon in El Born & Sant Pere — Browse the independent design boutiques and concept stores of El Born. Visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar again if you missed it, or explore the Parc de la Ciutadella for a shaded, relaxing stroll around the lake and the monumental cascade fountain (co-designed by a young Antoni Gaudí). Pick up souvenirs at local artisan shops rather than tourist traps on La Rambla.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Rooftop Send-Off — Celebrate the final evening with a special dinner followed by drinks at a rooftop bar. End the night with a walk along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia to admire the Modernista facades lit up at night — a magical final Barcelona memory.

meals.breakfast: El Xampanyet in El Born (opens late morning) for cava (Catalan sparkling wine) and tapas — a Barcelona institution. Or Bar Marsella in El Raval for a historic atmosphere with coffee and pastries.
meals.lunch: Espai Mescladís in El Born — a social enterprise restaurant with excellent Catalan-Mediterranean lunch menus (€13–16 menú del día) in a beautiful space. Supports local community employment.
meals.dinner: Moments at Mandarin Oriental (splurge option, €80–100/person) for a Michelin-starred farewell dinner on Passeig de Gràcia. Mid-range alternative: Cervecería Catalana or Parking Pizza revisited for a nostalgic final meal (€20–30/person). Follow dinner with rooftop cocktails at the Hotel Arts or W Barcelona for stunning nighttime skyline views.

day_by_day.notes: Palau de la Música tickets should be booked online in advance. Check the concert schedule — attending a live performance (jazz, classical, or flamenco) in the evening here would be a spectacular alternative to club nightlife on the last night (tickets €20–50). Pack and prepare for departure the following day — keep the evening relaxed enough to allow for an early start if needed.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via private luxury transfer (pre-booked black car service). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation stroll along Passeig de Gràcia from your Eixample base — admire the iconic 'Block of Discord' featuring Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller from the exterior. Stop at a terrace café for a welcome glass of cava. Pop into the Casa Batlló gift shop or book a late-afternoon Casa Batlló evening experience (Magic Nights) if available on arrival day.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona's late-night rhythm with a sophisticated dinner in Eixample, followed by cocktails at a rooftop bar. Experience the city's famous 'late dinner' culture — reservations at 21:00 are perfectly normal.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or skip — arrival is at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — iconic Eixample tapas bar beloved by locals and visitors alike; order the montaditos and patatas bravas. Arrive by 14:30 to beat the post-lunch rush.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars) — one of the world's top restaurants, located in Eixample. Book the tasting menu for a theatrical, avant-garde Catalan fine dining experience. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport private transfer before departure. Confirm Disfrutar reservation months ahead — it books out quickly. Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue. August in Barcelona is hot (28–33°C), so stay hydrated and carry sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Join a premium skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's awe-inspiring unfinished basilica. Opt for the tower access add-on for panoramic views over Barcelona. Spend approximately 2–2.5 hours exploring the Nativity and Passion facades, the luminous interior nave, and the crypt museum. The morning light through the stained glass on the eastern nave is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — Take a short taxi or private car to Park Güell. Explore the mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and Gaudí's former house (now a museum). Afterward, descend into the bohemian Gràcia neighborhood for a relaxed wander through its charming plazas — Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia are perfect for people-watching. Browse independent boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample to refresh, then head to the Gothic Quarter for an atmospheric evening walk before dinner. Explore the illuminated Roman walls and the Cathedral of Barcelona by night.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Federal Café (Carrer del Parlament) — a beloved specialty coffee and brunch spot near Eixample, known for its avocado toast and freshly baked pastries.
meals.lunch: La Pepita — a stylish montaditos and craft beer bar in Gràcia, perfect after Park Güell. Try the jamón ibérico and smoked salmon montaditos.
meals.dinner: Lasarte (3 Michelin stars) — Chef Martín Berasategui's Barcelona flagship in the Monument Hotel. Exceptional Basque-Catalan haute cuisine tasting menu. One of the finest dining experiences in Spain.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access tickets online in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Park Güell's uneven mosaic paths. The Gràcia neighborhood is very walkable and pleasantly shaded by narrow streets in the afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — Embark on a guided premium walking tour through Barcelona's medieval heart. Discover the Roman ruins beneath Plaça Nova, the Gothic Cathedral's cloister with its resident geese, the Plaça Reial, and the atmospheric Carrer del Bisbe bridge. Transition into El Born to admire the stunning iron-and-glass Mercat de Santa Caterina (Enric Miralles' mosaic roof is breathtaking) and the Santa Maria del Mar basilica — a masterpiece of Catalan Gothic architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience — Walk up La Rambla to Barcelona's legendary covered market. Join a curated premium food tour sampling fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, jamón ibérico, and local seasonal fruits. Follow with a private cooking class or vermouth tasting at a nearby bodega. Alternatively, explore the nearby MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) and CCCB for a cultural interlude.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach Club & Nightlife on Passeig Marítim — Head to Barceloneta beach for the quintessential Barcelona beach evening. Begin with sunset cocktails at a premium chiringuito (beach bar) such as La Cova Fumada or a rooftop at W Barcelona. As night falls, transition to the vibrant Passeig Marítim nightlife strip.

meals.breakfast: Hofmann Pastisseria (El Born area) — legendary Michelin-recommended pastry school bakery. Try the croissants, which are widely considered the best in Barcelona.
meals.lunch: Bar del Pla (El Born) — elegant yet casual Catalan bistro. Order the croquetes de bacallà (salt cod croquettes) and grilled razor clams.
meals.dinner: Bestial — sophisticated Mediterranean restaurant beneath the W Barcelona hotel, with outdoor terrace seating directly on Barceloneta beach. Perfect for a long, languid dinner watching the sea. Excellent grilled fish and seafood rice dishes.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is extremely crowded mid-morning — aim to arrive by 09:30 or after 14:00 for a better experience. The Gothic Quarter walk is best done in the morning before the heat peaks. Bring a light layer for the evening sea breeze at Barceloneta.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe — Take a private car or the Montjuïc cable car up to explore the hill's architectural gems. Visit the Barcelona Pavilion, Mies van der Rohe's seminal 1929 modernist masterpiece — a pilgrimage site for architecture lovers. Continue to the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert. Enjoy panoramic views over the city and port from the castle ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Architecture & Design Deep Dive — Return to Eixample for a curated self-guided or private-guided tour of Modernisme beyond Gaudí. Visit Casa Lleó Morera, Palau del Baró de Quadras, and the extraordinary Palau de la Música Catalana (UNESCO World Heritage Site) in El Born — Lluís Domènech i Montaner's flamboyant concert hall is one of the world's most beautiful interiors. Book a guided tour or, ideally, tickets to an evening concert.
day_by_day.evening: Upscale Eixample Nightlife — Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife scene. Start with pre-dinner cocktails at Dry Martini Bar (Carrer d'Aribau) — a Barcelona institution since 1978, with impeccable classic cocktails. After dinner, explore the 'Gayxample' area's sophisticated bars, or head to a jazz club such as Jamboree in Plaça Reial for live music.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume (Passeig de Gràcia) — elegant Eixample bakery and café. Enjoy ensaïmada pastry, fresh orange juice, and café amb llet (café con leche).
meals.lunch: Quimet & Quimet (Poble Sec, near Montjuïc) — legendary standing-room-only bodega famous for its creative montaditos and vermouth. A true Barcelona institution despite its tiny size.
meals.dinner: Alkimia (1 Michelin star) — Chef Jordi Vilà's refined modern Catalan cuisine in Eixample. The tasting menu reimagines traditional Catalan dishes with extraordinary precision and creativity.

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música Catalana tickets well in advance — both guided tours and evening concerts sell out. The Mies van der Rohe Pavilion opens at 10:00. Quimet & Quimet is only open for lunch (closed evenings and weekends afternoons) — plan accordingly. August evenings are warm enough to enjoy outdoor terrace dining until midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Pedrera (Casa Milà) Rooftop & Diagonal Luxury Shopping — Begin with a premium visit to Casa Milà (La Pedrera), Gaudí's last civil building and perhaps his most avant-garde. The rooftop warrior-chimney sculptures at golden hour are iconic. Book the 'La Pedrera by Night' experience if your flight allows, or enjoy the morning visit with full access to the Espai Gaudí exhibition. Afterward, stroll along Avinguda Diagonal and Passeig de Gràcia for luxury shopping — Loewe, Hermès, and local designer boutiques are all within walking distance of the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed Farewell Afternoon — Depending on flight time, enjoy a leisurely lunch and a final wander. Visit the Museu del Modernisme Català for a last dose of Catalan Art Nouveau. Alternatively, indulge in a spa treatment at your hotel or a nearby luxury spa. Begin packing and arrange private airport transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner or departure — If departing late, enjoy a final tapas crawl through Eixample's best bars. If departing the next day, experience one last night of Barcelona's extraordinary nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Brunch & Cake (Eixample) — a beloved brunch institution with creative, health-forward dishes and exceptional coffee.
meals.lunch: Parking Pizza (Carrer de de Londres, Eixample) — don't let the name deceive you; this is one of Barcelona's most acclaimed and stylish restaurants, with a stunning interior and exceptional wood-fired cuisine beyond just pizza. Book ahead.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Carrer de Sepúlveda) — intimate, candlelit wine bar and restaurant with a superb natural wine list and refined small plates. Perfect for a sentimental final evening in Eixample.

day_by_day.notes: La Pedrera rooftop is one of the most photographed spots in Barcelona — arrive at opening time (09:00) to beat crowds and heat. Confirm private airport transfer the evening before. Keep luggage at the hotel's concierge if checking out before your flight. Tip: purchase a bottle of cava from a local wine shop as a Barcelona souvenir.
